item.text: I’ll read the fixture, solve the scheduling problem, and check feasibility and optimality.

item.command:
/bin/zsh -lc "python3 -c 'import json,itertools
with open(\"input.json\") as f: data=json.load(f)
ops=sorted(data[\"operations\"],key=lambda o:o[\"id\"])
H=data[\"horizon\"]
ids=[o[\"id\"] for o in ops]
domains=[o[\"permitted_starts\"] if o[\"permitted_starts\"] is not None else range(H-o[\"duration\"]+1) for o in ops]
best=None
valid=0
for vec in itertools.product(*domains):
    starts=dict(zip(ids,vec))
    ends={o[\"id\"]:starts[o[\"id\"]]+o[\"duration\"] for o in ops}
    if any(starts[o[\"id\"]]<0 or ends[o[\"id\"]]>H or any(ends[p]>starts[o[\"id\"]] for p in o[\"requires\"]) for o in ops): continue
    if any(sum(o[\"demand\"].get(r,0) for o in ops if starts[o[\"id\"]]<=t<ends[o[\"id\"]])>cap for r,cap in data[\"capacities\"].items() for t in range(H)): continue
    valid+=1
    score=(max(ends.values()),sum(starts[o[\"id\"]]*o[\"risk_weight\"] for o in ops),vec)
    if best is None or score<best: best=score
print(json.dumps({\"feasible_schedules\":valid,\"starts\":dict(zip(ids,best[2])),\"makespan\":best[0],\"risk_exposure\":best[1]}))'"
